Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

different adjective

also differently, unlike, not the same, different from

classical

Ter. Ph. 684: aliud mihi respondēs ac rogō?
Sall. Cat. 6.2: alius aliō mōre vīventēs
Ter. And. 189: nunc hic diēs aliam vītam affert, aliōs mōrēs postulat

alius, alia, aliud

adjective and pronoun; “different from” is alius ac (atque)

other, different

Latin says “different” with alius: alius ac (atque) is “different from”; aliud est … aliud … is “… is one thing, … another”; and a doubled alius gives “each a different …”: alius aliō mōre, each in a different way.

Examples

  • Eho, verberō, aliud mihi respondēs ac rogō?

    Hey, you rascal, you’re answering something different from what I asked?Ter. Ph. 684

  • aliud est properāre, aliud festīnāre

    hurrying is one thing, rushing anotherCato in Gell. 16.14.2

  • disparī genere, dissimilī linguā, alius aliō mōre vīventēs

    of different stock and different speech, each living in a different waySall. Cat. 6.2

  • nōn vidēs quam dīversus sit dēscendentium habitus et ēscendentium?

    don’t you see how differently people carry themselves going down and going up?Sen. Ep. 123.14

Other words

  • aliter — differently, otherwise

    adverb; “differently from” is aliter ac (atque) · also used · classical · Verg. A. 2.428: dīs aliter vīsum; Cic. Fam. 3.7.5: tū sī aliter exīstimās, “if you think differently”

  • dīversus, dīversa, dīversum — different, opposite; going different ways

    also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 123.14; Tac. Ann. 6.28: ā cēterīs avibus dīversum

    Stronger than alius: turned the other way, contrary.

  • dissimilis, dissimile — unlike, dissimilar

    adjective, with a genitive or dative · also used · classical · Sall. Cat. 6.2: dissimilī linguā; Cic.; Hor. (Lewis & Short)

  • differō, differre, distulī, dīlātum — differ, be different

    verb, irregular; intransitive in this sense, with ab · also used · classical · Cic. Caecin. 39: quid hoc ab illō differt?

    Transitive, the same verb means “put off”, “postpone”.

SourcesLewis & Short: alius · Lewis & Short: aliter · Lewis & Short: diverto (dīversus) · Lewis & Short: dissimilis · Lewis & Short: differo
